QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_12

question.text: 'Vindhya Growth Category II AIF' holds a minority 25% stake in an investee company and negotiates a DRAG-ALONG right on the promoters. The primary purpose of this right is to:

answer.text: Force the promoters to sell their shares alongside the AIF on the same terms, so a potential buyer can acquire a control stake and pay a strategic premium
Prevent the promoters from ever selling their shares
Ensure the AIF receives 2x of its investment on exit
Give the AIF a veto over the company's dividend declaration

explanation.text: The Logic: Drag-along lets a minority investor 'drag' the promoters into a joint sale so the combined stake is large enough to attract a potential buyer who can acquire a control stake and pay a strategic premium. The Trap: Drag does not prevent promoter sale; it compels parallel sale. A 2x recovery is liquidation preference, and a veto on dividends is a different protective provision. Note: The workbook supports drag-along rights on promoters so a minority AIF can offer a larger stake and attract a control or strategic premium in M&A exits. Cat III, price-floor, IRR, reputation, and court/litigation commentary have been removed as not source-supported.
